title: The Bath of the Nymph over the bed. Given away with the Easter number of Photo Bits: Splendid masterpiece in art colours. Tea before you put milk in. Not unlike her with her hair down: slimmer. Three and six I gave for the frame. She said it would look nice over the bed. Naked nymphs: Greece: and for instance all the people that lived then.
html_source:
An allusion to Titian’s famous painting of the story of Actaeon, which features nude bathing nymphs. This sort of contrast between Bloom weighing the price, and remembering the sort of chintzy way in which he acquired the painting, and the high art of it continues the mixture of intellectual contemplation and the daily grind.

Also, this is another of the mythological motifs present throughout the book.

He turned the pages back. 

 — Metempsychosis, he said, is what the ancient Greeks called it. They used to believe you could be changed into an animal or a tree, for instance.
